gating_rule: The agent MUST NOT set state=passing. Only the harness may, after running `verification` and capturing exit code 0. States: planned (not built) | spiked (design validated cross-OS by a passing spike; real impl + test pending) | accepted (decision/meta-criterion met) | passing (harness-only, terminal).

features.behavior: With `hive serve` running, >=2 concurrent client sessions complete vault reads/writes through it and exactly one hive daemon process owns the SQLite DBs + git working tree.
features.evidence: Implemented in slice 3 as a real vault+git multi-client test: 2 concurrent `hive client` shims append to the same file through one daemon -> all 8 writes land (no lost updates) and the daemon owns the git history (9 commits = init + 2x4, one per append, deterministic across 3 runs). No new production code needed: the single-owner daemon turns the old inter-process write filelock into an intra-process threading.Lock. Pre-validated cross-OS by spike/load_spike.py (4/4 Linux+Windows). Awaiting harness pass-state.

features.behavior: A single call (`hive status` / `/status` / extended `worker_status`) returns metrics aggregated across >=2 sessions and persists across a session disconnect.
With no daemon running, a client call still succeeds via in-process stdio and the response/health flags degraded (non-daemon) mode.
features.evidence: Implemented in slice 2 (src/hive/_client.py: `hive client` shim falls back to in-process create_server() when no live daemon is reachable). Tests green locally via `make check` (exit 0): test_client_falls_back_without_daemon (no state files) + test_client_falls_back_on_stale_state (dead port behind stale state). Degraded mode surfaced via the `hive.client.mode=fallback reason={no_daemon_state,daemon_unreachable}` startup log. Awaiting harness pass-state.

features.behavior: Loopback Streamable-HTTP + per-daemon bearer token round-trips a tools/call and rejects missing/wrong tokens (401) on Linux AND Windows.
features.evidence: transport_spike 5/5 on Linux AND Windows (2026-05-31). To become a pytest integration test in the cross-OS CI lane.

features.ac: Local transport is owner-gated by token
features.behavior: The token file is owner-only (POSIX 0600 / Windows icacls ACL) and a request without the matching token is refused.
features.evidence: transport_spike owner-only + 401 checks pass on Linux AND Windows (2026-05-31).

features.behavior: A vault_write/patch carries an idempotency key; a retried key is a no-op (at-most-once), safe for append mode, including under concurrency.
features.evidence: idempotency_spike 3/3 on Linux AND Windows (2026-05-31), incl. 12 concurrent duplicates -> one row. Real impl wires the key through the tool envelope + a shared applied-key store.

features.behavior: Killing the daemon (SIGKILL) triggers supervisor auto-restart; durable state (SQLite + git) is intact, and in-flight clients reconnect or fall back.
features.evidence: Crash-only durability pre-validated by spike/resilience_spike.py 4/4 (Linux+Windows): state durable + integrity_check=ok after SIGKILL/TerminateProcess, reconnect, disconnect survival. The supervisor (systemd/launchd unit) itself is post-build.

features.behavior: An abnormal exit writes a crash artifact (last-N ring buffer, lock/DB state, in-flight requests, version, traceback) with NO secrets/API keys (ADR-011 §6.3 redaction).
Every request is logged once with a correlation_id + session_id traceable across the daemon log and metrics; one daemon log replaces per-PID files.
Live metrics served from memory (no synchronous per-call DB write on the hot path); forensic JSON-lines + crash artifact; historical telemetry in usage.db surviving a restart.
A large (1 MB) payload round-trips intact; missing/empty/wrong-scheme auth are all rejected; a port-in-use daemon exits cleanly.
ADR-011 captures the daemon decision, transport choice, fallback contract, resilience/observability design, and what it supersedes in ADR-005.
features.evidence: ADR-011 status: accepted (2026-05-31). Merges with the HIVE-118 PR.
